in.intro: For machines on the LAN (NAS, servers, dev machines). Run one command on the device and the agent connects to the hub with a pairing code. All settings are managed here; no secrets are stored on the device.
in.name: Name
in.nameHelp: Up to 64 characters. Leave empty to use the hostname reported by the agent.
in.roleHelp: The role only groups devices and picks icons; it does not change behavior. Dev machines default to Allow offline.
in.allowOfflineOn: Shown as Dormant when offline, no alert
in.allowOfflineOff: Shown as Offline with an alert
in.allowOfflineHelp: For laptops that are often powered off: when on, offline shows as a gray Dormant state without alerts.
in.autoMetricsHint: Creates a host-metrics instance on the device after it connects
in.hubMeta: The agent must be able to reach this address
in.hubHelp: A device that cannot resolve the address will fail to connect; across subnets pick the one that routes.
in.oneTitle: One line · detects OS and architecture, verifies SHA-256, then installs
in.oneNoteDev: Dev machines (macOS) use user mode and the script drops sudo; on a Linux dev machine append --user to the command.
in.oneNote: Linux system mode needs root and the script will ask for sudo; macOS automatically uses user mode.
in.step3: 3 · Verify SHA-256 (sha256sum on Linux, shasum -a 256 on macOS)
in.step4: 4 · Install (sudo on Linux, user mode on macOS)
in.stepsNote: The checksum and binary come from the same HTTP address, which only guards against corruption; use the HTTPS access address if that is not enough.
in.sudoersHint: For disk SMART and other storage health data, add {{flag}} at the end of the command.
in.noEmbed: This hub has no embedded agent, so the one-line and download commands will not work. Get the agent from GitHub Releases and install it by hand; the commands are shown as usual.
in.codeHelp: Valid for 15 minutes and single use; after it expires choose Edit to generate a new one.
in.fingerprintHelp: The agent trusts only this public key fingerprint (pinning), not a CA. It is already in the one-line command; for step-by-step installs compare it with the terminal output.
in.optionalHelp: To monitor Docker or storage health, append --docker-group or --sudoers to the command (curl | sh is non-interactive, so they must be explicit).
in.waiting: Waiting for the agent to connect…
in.expiredHint: Choose Edit to generate a new pairing code.
in.expiredHintRepair: Choose Regenerate to get a new pairing code.
in.codeHelpRepair: Valid for 15 minutes and single use; after it expires choose Regenerate.
in.foundNotOnline: The device for this pairing was found as "{{name}}" but is not online yet ({{status}})

out.step1: Install on the VPS and open the pairing window
out.step1Body: A VPS is not on your LAN, so the hub connects out to it: install the agent on the VPS in listening mode, then run pimon-agent pair to open a 15-minute pairing window; it prints the SPKI fingerprint and pairing code.
out.downloadTitle: Download from GitHub Releases and verify SHA-256
out.installTitle: Install in listening mode, then open the pairing window
out.noRelease: This is a development build with no matching GitHub Release, so the download command is hidden. Put the agent binary on the VPS yourself, then run install --listen and pair.
out.tipFirewall: Open TCP {{port}} (the --listen port) in the security group and firewall, allowing only the hub's egress IP; if the hub dials through a proxy, use the proxy's egress IP.
out.tipWindow: Each pairing window lasts 15 minutes and closes after one successful pairing; after it expires run sudo pimon-agent pair again.
out.addressHelp: Format host:port; wss:// is added automatically. Use the VPS public address, not the LAN IP printed by pair.
out.fingerprintHelp: Format SHA256:<base64>; compare it character by character with the SPKI fingerprint printed by pair.
out.proxyHelp: Which global proxy the hub uses to reach the VPS; manage them on the Proxies page.
out.name: Name
out.autoMetricsHint: Creates a host-metrics instance on the device after pairing
out.progressSteps: Connecting to the VPS (through the proxy if selected); checking the SPKI fingerprint; submitting the pairing code and waiting for the agent

unreachable.tip1: Open TCP {{port}} in the cloud security group and the system firewall, allowing the hub's (or proxy's) egress IP.
unreachable.tip2: Use the VPS public address, with the same port as --listen (host:port).
unreachable.tip3: On the VPS run sudo pimon-agent status to confirm the agent is running in listening mode.
unreachable.tip4: If you picked a proxy, test on the Proxies page that it can reach this address.

pin_mismatch.tip1: Compare the SPKI fingerprint printed by pimon-agent pair character by character, including the SHA256: prefix.
pin_mismatch.tip2: Reinstalling the VPS or regenerating its certificate changes the fingerprint; once you are sure it is your machine, enter the new one.
pin_mismatch.tip3: If it never matches, someone may be impersonating the VPS; try another network path.

code_expired.tip1: Run sudo pimon-agent pair on the VPS again to get a new fingerprint and pairing code.
code_expired.tip2: Enter the new code in the form above and choose Pair and add again.

bad_code.tip1: Check the pairing code character by character; separators are optional and case is ignored.
bad_code.tip2: A code works only once; if it was already used, run sudo pimon-agent pair on the VPS again.

rate_limited.tip1: The agent caps failed attempts per source and has locked this one for a while; try again in about fifteen minutes.
rate_limited.tip2: Check the address, fingerprint and code first so you do not trigger the lock again.

incompatible.tip1: The device is kept in the device list and joins automatically once the agent is upgraded.

timeout.tip1: Check the network from the hub to the VPS, and the proxy if one is used.
timeout.tip2: Make sure the agent is running on the VPS; run sudo pimon-agent pair again if needed and retry.

unknown.tip1: Open the System page and look in the hub log for why this pairing failed.
unknown.tip2: Check the address, fingerprint and code, then retry.

address.invalid: Bad address format: use host:port or wss://host:port (write IPv6 as [address]:port)

fingerprint.invalid: The fingerprint must look like SHA256:<base64>; compare it with the pair output

code.invalid: Bad pairing code format; compare it with the pair output

revoke.title: Revoke device "{{name}}"?
revoke.body: Revoking invalidates the device credential at once, drops its session and stops the agent from reconnecting (to bring it back you must pair again). Instances on the device are kept: their location shows "Reference lost" and collection is paused until you pick a new location for them.

repair.why2: You suspect the credential leaked and want the old one invalidated at once
repair.why3: A different machine replaces this device: instances, device settings and maintenance mode move to the new device, and the old device is replaced once pairing succeeds
repair.repinIn: If only the hub certificate was rebuilt (the fingerprint changed) you do not need to re-pair: run {{cmd}} on the device to update the pin (dial-in devices only).
repair.outNote: If the VPS only changed IP or port and the certificate is the same, change the address under Properties; no re-pairing needed. If the agent was reinstalled on the VPS and the certificate changed, re-pair here with the new fingerprint and pairing code.

repair.replaced: Re-pairing finished: the old device was replaced by the new one

history.title: Version history
history.brokenTitle: This version has widgets with broken references
history.confirmBody: This creates a new version v{{next}} with the content of v{{v}}; intermediate versions are not deleted.
history.confirmDirty: You have {{n}} unsaved change(s); they will be lost after the rollback.
history.confirmBroken: {{n}} widget(s) in this version have broken references and will show as placeholders after the rollback:

broken.instance_missing: The bound instance no longer exists
broken.instance_plugin_mismatch: The instance does not belong to the widget's plugin
broken.widget_missing: The plugin no longer provides this widget
broken.size_unsupported: The plugin no longer provides this size

outOfBounds.title: Shrinking to {{cols}}×{{rows}} puts {{n}} widget(s) out of bounds
outOfBounds.body: The widgets below do not fit the new grid; continuing removes them from the layout.

screens.sub: The index home page plus any number of screens, one grid per screen
screens.saveInvalid: The layout is invalid ({{n}} problems). Please check and try again
screens.dirtyHint: Based on v{{base}} · saving layout changes creates v{{next}} and pushes it to the display
screens.conflict: The layout was changed elsewhere: you are on v{{base}}, the latest is v{{latest}}. Reloading discards the unsaved changes on this page.

leave.title: Leave screen management?
leave.body: There are unsaved changes that will be lost.

chg.order: Changed the rotation order of the screens
chg.display: Screen display options (rotation, input mode, UI scale or daily restart)

rotation.title: Rotation
rotation.homeOnlyDesc: Other screens can only be switched remotely.
rotation.autoDesc: Rotate the participating screens in the order listed below.
rotation.noTouchWarn: This display has no touch: with "Home page only", other screens can only be switched from Remote control, and there is no way to page by hand on the display.
rotation.idleHelp: After switching remotely to another screen, how long without interaction before returning to index.

grid.title: Grid
grid.label: Columns × rows
grid.help: Presets match 800×480 · 1024×600 · 1280×720; ★ is the one recommended for the display. When shrinking the grid, widgets that no longer fit are removed after you confirm.

list.title: Screens
list.meta: Drag the handle to change the rotation order · index stays on top
list.dragHint: Drag to reorder; Up and Down arrow keys on the handle also work
list.dwellInvalid: Dwell must be a whole number of seconds from {{min}} to {{max}}; leave empty for the default

delete.title: Delete screen {{id}}?
delete.body: Screen "{{name}}" and its {{n}} widgets will be removed from the layout once you save; the version history can still roll it back.

input.title: Display input
input.label: Input mode
input.detectedNone: The display has not reported touch capability yet.
input.help: Without touch the display shows no paging hint; rotation and remote switching are unaffected.

scale.title: UI scale
scale.label: Scale
scale.help: Enlarges text and spacing on high-resolution displays; the grid columns × rows stay the same.
scale.restart: After saving, the kiosk on this device restarts Chromium automatically and the scale takes effect.

screens.settingsFailedAfterLayout: The layout was saved (v{{version}}), but saving the settings failed: {{error}}

restart.title: Daily restart
restart.label: Restart browser daily
restart.help: Off by default. Only the kiosk Chromium browser restarts, not the hub or the Raspberry Pi; the time follows the timezone in settings.

remote.sub: Without touching the screen: refresh, switch, power
remote.offlineHint: The display is offline: refresh and switch screen are unavailable. Power on, power off and wake apply once the display reconnects.

reason.remote_on: Turned on remotely until {{until}} (the next period boundary), then back to the schedule.
reason.remote_off: Turned off remotely until {{until}} (the next period boundary), then back to the schedule.
reason.wake: Temporarily lit; back to the schedule when it ends at {{until}}.
reason.remote_on_open: Turned on remotely until the next period boundary, then back to the schedule.
reason.remote_off_open: Turned off remotely until the next period boundary, then back to the schedule.
reason.wake_open: Temporarily lit; back to the schedule when it ends.

keys.title: Keys
keys.meta: k1–k6 · sent to the kiosk right away

refresh.label: Refresh
refresh.desc: Reload the screen page; layout and data update immediately.

switch.label: Switch screen
switch.desc: Go to the target screen; back to the home screen after {{n}} s idle.

on.label: Power on
on.desc: Light the screen until the next schedule boundary, then follow the schedule again.

off.label: Power off
off.desc: Turn the display off until the next schedule boundary, then follow the schedule again.

wake.label: Temporary wake
wake.desc: Light the screen during an off period; it returns to the schedule when time is up.

token.label: Reset screen token
token.desc: The old token stops working at once; the kiosk on this device signs in again automatically, while screens on other devices must be reopened with the new token.

token.title: Reset the screen token?
token.warn: The old token stops working at once; the screen is disconnected and shows "Screen token invalid".
token.consequence: The kiosk on this device signs in again with the new token within seconds. Screens on other devices must be reopened with the new token link, and stay on their last frame until then.
token.doneBody: The new token was written to the screen.token file in the hub data directory. The kiosk on this device signs in again automatically; for screens on other devices, open this link to sign in again:
token.doneHint: Only needed on other devices: replace <token> with the contents of screen.token (a single line of text).

schedule.sub: The screen switches theme or turns off by period, in the global time zone

leave.title: Leave the schedule?
leave.body: The schedule or Reduce effects has unsaved changes that will be lost.

schedule.override: A remote action currently controls the screen; the schedule takes over again when it ends.

tl.title: 24-hour timeline
tl.meta: click a block to select · drag or use arrow keys to move boundaries · pick a theme below
tl.handle: Adjust the boundary at {{time}} (arrow keys ±5 min, Shift+arrow ±1 h)

list.title: Periods
list.deleted: Period deleted; the previous one now ends at {{time}}
list.addHint: A new period is cut out of the one it falls in, so the timeline always covers 24 hours.
list.tooShort: This period is too short to split

edit.title: Edit period {{n}}
edit.hintOff: Off periods have no theme; see 02.5 for wake rules
edit.linked: Changing a start or end time moves the neighbouring boundary too, so periods stay edge to edge.

problems.title: The schedule is invalid and must be fixed before saving
problems.theme: Theme is not a built-in theme or off
problems.empty: At least one period is required
problems.gap: {{from}}–{{to}} is not covered by any period

reduce.title: Reduce effects
reduce.help: Turns off glow and motion; good for always-on use or weak hardware. Same switch as Settings · Display.
reduce.settingsFailedAfterPlan: The schedule was saved but Reduce effects could not be saved: {{error}}

wake.title: Wake rules
wake.critSub: Lights for 10 minutes, then off again
wake.touchSub: Tap the screen to light it when touch is present

upload_reason.not_writable: Directory cannot be created or is not writable
upload_reason.io: Read/write error on the remote, or no progress for too long
upload_reason.canceled: Upload canceled because the hub was shutting down
upload_reason.cleanup_failed: Uploaded, but removing expired remote backups failed
